input.brief: Crocs annual marketing plan: playful comfort, foam clogs, Jibbitz customization, mass-market irreverence, subscription strategy

direction.name: The object, large
direction.idea: Show the thing, bigger than seems reasonable. One photographed object fills the first screen, scaled until the viewport crops it, with the text small and tucked beside or behind it. The crop is the idea: a record whose edge leaves the top-right corner, a bottle whose shoulder runs off the bottom, a chair seen so close you read its grain. Being that close reads as confidence in the object. Everything else on the page serves it: details as tight close-ups, facts as short lines, one way to buy.
direction.composition: First screen: the object occupies 55–75% of the viewport and breaks at least one edge. It sits on a flat field (ground colour or one bold colour), never in a box. The headline is short and either very large and partly hidden behind the object (10–13vw, the object overlapping two or three letters) or small (28–36px) in the opposite corner with a one-line description. No navigation bar beyond a wordmark and one action. Following sections: a row of three or four close-up details at different crop ratios (not equal tiles), a single wide photograph of the object in use, a plain list of facts set large (materials, size, price) aligned to one edge, then the purchase action. The object returns once at the end from a different angle.
direction.typography: Either very large and structural or very small and precise; pick one for the headline and hold it. Facts are set in the text face at 22–28px, not in a table.
direction.colour: A flat field chosen to make the object's own colour sing (its complement, or a tone darker than its shadow side). One field for the whole page, or a second for the facts section.
direction.imagery: Use the product's own photographs if they exist. Otherwise use a still-life from the dealt set as a stand-in and say so. Prefer images with a plain background; use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` on light fields so a white studio background disappears into the page colour.
direction.photoTreatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.
direction.richness: The object's surface at close range, and the tension of the crop.
direction.pitfalls: A small centred product shot with space all round is a catalogue thumbnail, not this direction. If the image has a busy background it cannot sit on a field; crop tighter or change image. Keep text off the object's focal area.

hero.name: Object splits the headline
hero.blueprint: One deep, flat ground colour. The object, a low-key studio photograph whose background matches the ground, stands at dead centre, scaled to 66% of the viewport height and tilted about 8 degrees, with its base cropped by the bottom edge. The headline is split around it: line one is centred across the object's upper fifth and line two across its lower fifth, both at clamp(64px, 5.8vw, 92px), regular weight, spanning columns 2–11, so the object fills the gap where a paragraph would normally sit. The type lies above the object in the stacking order in the light ink, so every letter stays readable where it crosses. At the object's mid-height two small text blocks at 14px face each other: the supporting sentence far left on columns 1–2, and two short facts (size, price) far right on columns 11–12, right-aligned, each 32px from its edge. Wordmark top-left; three text links top-centre; the single action top-right as a small light rectangular tab, the only light solid on the screen. The lower corners stay dark and empty.
hero.mobile: The object is 54svh tall, centred, its base cropped by the bottom edge. Line one of the headline crosses its top at 11vw and line two its lower third at 11vw, both centred inside 16px margins. The side text blocks merge into one 15px sentence under the navigation. Wordmark top-left and the action tab top-right; the links collapse to one word.
hero.headline: A two-line statement of four to six words, up to about 16 characters per line at 5.8vw, with the object standing between the lines.

type.note: A slightly narrow neo-grotesk with closed apertures, used at regular weight from marquee size down to paragraphs. Suits agencies and digital studios that want large type without heaviness.

palette.name: Swapping pastels
palette.note: One flat pastel is the whole background and it swaps per project or chapter: periwinkle, pink, sand, sage, peach. Type and one solid box stay near-black on all five, and dark teal is only for the button.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Narrow column, empty field
sections.blueprint: A single text column 300–340px wide, its left edge at 15% of the viewport width, starting 64px below the section top. It holds four or five short paragraphs at 15–16px with leading 1.5 and one blank line between them; the first paragraph is in medium weight and full ink, the rest in regular weight and the soft ink. No heading, no image, no button; one underlined text link may end the last paragraph. The remaining three-quarters of the 1440 screen is untouched ground, and the section is only as tall as the text plus 160px of padding below. The column's left edge must match a line used elsewhere on the page (the wordmark's left edge or a later column). Where the page has a large object or a fixed photograph, this column is the small text beside it. Holds 90–150 words comfortably.
sections.mobile: The column becomes 78% of the width, left-aligned at the 20px margin, so a strip of empty ground remains on the right as a deliberate margin. Text stays at 15–16px with the first paragraph in medium weight. Padding is 72px above and 96px below.

sections.name: Figure on the photograph's edge
sections.blueprint: One full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 88svh, and one figure set on it the way a film title sits on a frame. The figure, with its unit, is at clamp(120px, 17vw, 280px), leading 0.8, in paper colour, hugging the bottom-left corner with 24px margins, its baseline nearly on the photograph's lower edge. A neutral dark scrim covers only the bottom 35% of the image for legibility. On the same baseline at the right margin, right-aligned, a sentence of up to 26ch at 18px explains the figure. At the top-left, small at 20–24px, sits the heading of two to four words; the middle of the photograph stays clear. Two smaller supporting figures may follow below the photograph, on the ground: each at 40px with a one-line caption beside it, starting at columns 1 and 7, 40px under the image. Choose a figure that belongs to the picture: a height, a distance, a temperature, a year.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 80svh, cropped to its subject. The figure sits bottom-left at 30vw; the sentence moves above it at 16px, left-aligned. Supporting figures stack under the photograph at 32px, each with its caption on the line beneath.

sections.name: Names running off the edges
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed band in a flat colour, about 34vh tall, holding a single line of names that is cropped by both viewport edges. The names are set at 8vw in the display weight, `white-space: nowrap`, separated by a solid round dot one third of the cap height, and the line moves slowly to the left (a CSS `translateX` animation over 40 seconds on a duplicated track, paused under `prefers-reduced-motion`). The band has no heading. Its meaning comes from one sentence at 18px set directly below the band at the left margin on the page ground, stating plainly who these names are. Supplied logos may replace names if all are available as single-colour SVGs at 0.8em height; do not mix logos and set names in one line. The band butts against the sections above and below with no gap.
sections.mobile: The band is 22vh tall with names at 15vw, still cropped at both edges and still moving. The explaining sentence sits under it at 16px with 20px margins. Do not add a second line running the opposite way; one line is the idea.

sections.name: Two objects, two fields
sections.blueprint: Two panels side by side, each 50vw wide and 92svh tall, in two different flat tones from the palette, meeting on a clean vertical edge with no gap. Each panel is dominated by one cut-out object photograph scaled to 130–150% of the panel's width and positioned so the panel's top edge crops it: the reader sees the lower two-thirds of the object, very close. On light panels use mix-blend-mode: multiply to lose a white studio background. Along the bottom of each panel, 28px in from the edges, one row: the name at 20px medium and a price or fact at 17px on the left; on the right, two small rectangular actions, one filled with ink and one with paper. Nothing sits in the middle of a panel. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, is set at the top-left of the first panel only, in the empty corner beside the object.
sections.mobile: Panels stack, each 78svh tall, the object scaled to 150% of the width and cut by the top and right edges. The bottom row becomes two lines: name and fact, then the two actions side by side at full width. The heading sits top-left on the first panel at 26px.

sections.name: Two-column menu, photo bullets
sections.blueprint: A menu or catalogue list in which each item has a small cut-out photograph where a bullet would be. Each category opens with its name at clamp(32px, 3.4vw, 50px) at the left margin and the number of items at 16px right-aligned on the same baseline, with 96px above and 40px below. Items then run in two columns with a 64px gutter and 36px between rows. Each item is a two-part row: a 64px photograph of the item on a plain background at the left (multiplied onto the ground with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, or masked to the page's one shape), then 20px to its right the name in bold at 17–18px with the price right-aligned on the same line, and beneath it a two- or three-line description at 15px in the soft ink, max 38ch. A short note such as an allergen follows the description in the accent ink. No boxes. Holds 6–10 items per category.
sections.mobile: One column. Photographs shrink to 52px and stay at the left; name and price share the first line with the description beneath at 15px. Category names at 8.5vw with the count on the same baseline. A sticky row of category names as text links lets the reader jump.

sections.name: The object returns
sections.blueprint: The thing shown in the hero comes back once, from another angle, to close the page. On one flat field 90svh tall, the object's photograph occupies columns 1–8, scaled to about 130% of that area and anchored so the section's bottom and left edges crop it (`overflow: hidden` on the section; on light fields `mix-blend-mode: multiply` removes a white studio background). The text sits small in columns 10–12, vertically centred: a closing line of three to five words at 32–40px, one sentence at 17px, the price or key fact on its own line at 22px, and one rectangular button. Nothing overlaps the object's focal area. Where the page's subject is a shape rather than a photograph, the page's motif takes the object's place at the same scale as a flat filled shape. The closing line is the only heading.
sections.mobile: The text block comes first: closing line at 28px, sentence, fact, full-width button. The object follows at 130% of the screen width, shifted so the right and bottom edges crop it, filling about 55svh on the same flat field.

references.name: Aevion
references.idea: One photoreal drone flies down the whole page through a white space organised only by hairlines and very light type.
references.hero: The first capture is the preloader: a white field with a tiny mono percentage counter dead centre. The loaded hero is white with a hairline-thin top bar: logo and a descriptor left, a credit and a live GMT clock in the middle, a small grey menu chip right. A pale blue-grey gradient panel fills the top 40% inside 12px margins. A white 3D drone hovers at centre, straddling a full-width hairline; a vertical hairline drops from it to the bottom edge. The headline is only 24px, two lines, far left, sitting on the horizontal rule with its second sentence greyed; a scroll cue sits far right on the same line.
references.type: Switzer in light weight (300) with -0.033em tracking for everything from the 24px headline to a single word at 16.7vw; protoMono at 12px in caps for bracketed labels and legal lines. Slate and pale grey mixed within one sentence. Four sizes.
references.colour: #fdfdfd #eef1f3 #24363f #a3abb0 #d5d9db — White on white with dark slate type and a paler grey for unrevealed words. The only tint is a faint blue-grey wash in the hero and the teal glint of the drone's lens. Cool.
references.imagery: A single white-and-grey quadcopter rendered live, with motion-blurred rotors, shown from front, three-quarter and side as it moves; often cropped by the right edge. Supporting graphics are hairline arcs and circles like a technical drawing.
references.layout: 12px page margins, content hung on a few full-width and half-width hairlines. Each screen holds one idea: a statement, a word, an object. Text stays left or lower-right while the drone travels between them. Nineteen screens of mostly white.

sections.description: White screen with a vertical hairline at 50% and a horizontal one near the bottom. Left half: a four-line statement at about 3vw in light grotesk, each word either dark slate or pale grey as a scroll-linked reveal passes through it. Right half: the drone in three-quarter view, cropped by the right edge and crossing the vertical rule.

A single noun set at 16.7vw in slate, top-left, the largest type on the page. A tiny mono label with a bullet sits far left at mid-height; a numbered chip sits top-right. The drone overlaps the right side at mid-height, and beneath it a 24px two-paragraph spec block occupies the right half, its later words still ghosted.

Landing diagram: the drone hovers above a drawing made only of hairlines: a large semicircular arc, a small circular target on the baseline, vertical dividers creating three bays, and a bracketed mono label above the target. Nothing else is on screen; the object and the drawing carry the whole frame.

Bracketed mono labels at both ends of a hairline, then a two-column row: a question at left, an answer plus a small square-cornered slate button at right. Below right, two short link lists in 12px; studio logo bottom-left; a mono legal line across the bottom edge.

steal: Use one hairline cross (a horizontal plus a vertical rule) as the only layout furniture and let the product render straddle it.
Set a single noun at 16vw as a chapter title and keep all explanatory copy at 24px, with nothing in between.
Reveal paragraphs word by word from pale grey to dark slate tied to scroll, so unread text stays visibly ghosted.

references.name: ARCHIV
references.idea: A waitlist page as a museum plinth: one cut-out everyday object at a time, centred on off-white beneath a heavy serif wordmark.
references.hero: Off-white single screen with no scroll. A heavy high-contrast serif wordmark in black caps sits top-left at a 56px margin, about 410px wide (28% of the viewport) and 80px tall. Opposite, top-right at the same margin, one line of 14px sans description aligns with the wordmark's top. Dead centre, one photographed object (a painted wooden pepper mill about 140px wide and 440px tall) stands on a barely visible lighter rounded square with a soft contact shadow; other objects replace it in turn. Below, a centred 11px grey line, then a white rounded email field 236px wide with a circled arrow inside its right end. Roughly 80% is empty.
references.type: The wordmark is drawn lettering in a heavy display serif with tight spacing, cap height about 5.5vw. All live text is Helvetica Neue regular at 14px and about 11px, black or grey. Two text sizes only; the contrast is wordmark against near-invisible interface text.
references.colour: #f1efec #000000 #ffffff #d9261c #e8a317 #7a7a75 — Warm off-white field, black wordmark, a white input; all colour arrives through whichever object is showing (red and yellow mill, tan leather, blue cap).
references.imagery: Studio cut-outs of single everyday objects in three-quarter view with a soft grounded shadow on matching off-white, each scaled to similar visual mass and centred, one at a time, no frame.
references.layout: One fixed viewport with four elements: wordmark top-left, description top-right, object in the exact centre, form bottom-centre. Margins of 56px, no rules, nav or footer. On mobile the wordmark centres and the description disappears.

sections.description: The central object rotates through unrelated things (pepper mill, sling chair, sticker-covered hydrant, layered iced drink, record player, baseball cap), each photographed in the same light and replaced in place within a zone roughly 250-300px square. Shadow direction and visual weight stay constant, so the object is the page's only variable and no carousel controls are needed.

Beneath the object, a centred line of 11px grey text, a 30px gap, then a white field about 236 by 52px with 12px radius: light grey placeholder at left and a 26px circle-outlined arrow as the submit control inside the right end. No button label, border or shadow; the field is the only pure white on the page, which marks it as the one interactive thing.

steal: Build a pre-launch page from four elements only (wordmark top-left, one-line description top-right, a single centred object, an email field) and leave the rest of the screen empty.
Cycle one consistently lit cut-out object in the same spot to show range without adding a grid or carousel controls.
Make the email field the only pure-white element on an off-white page, with submit as a circled arrow inside it rather than a labelled button.

references.name: Serotoninn
references.idea: A torn-paper seam splits the page in two, colour on white against greyscale on grey paper, to stage the brand's glam-versus-grunge line, with ultra-condensed heavy type straddling the tear.
references.hero: The viewport is split by a vertical torn-paper edge at 50%: left half pure white, right half a grey paper texture. A cut-out model stands dead centre, about 28% wide, running from 15% down off the bottom edge; her left half is full colour, her right half greyscale, the tear passing through her. Type is ultra-condensed heavy uppercase: the brand name at about 5.5vw top-left beneath a three-line mono menu; a two-line tagline right-aligned at mid-height on the right; and at bottom centre a two-word line at 8.2vw, first word red and second white, overlapping the dress, with a bracketed link beneath. Small centred logo at top, three mono links top-right.
references.type: Thunder extra-bold in uppercase, set tight, for all display lines (118px in the hero, similar for category words, sometimes rotated 90 degrees). PP Fraktion Mono uppercase at about 11px for nav, labels and prices; Inter for small body. Square brackets and parentheses wrap secondary words and counts.
references.colour: #fdfdfd #d8d8d8 #0a0a0a #e8352b #fff9f7 #2a2fb0 — White, paper grey and black with red as the single interface accent (one headline word, section labels). Garment colour (cobalt, yellow, satin tan) supplies the rest. One full black campaign band.
references.imagery: Studio fashion photography of models, cut out or on white seamless, in tall portrait crops. The hero splits one image into colour and greyscale along a torn-paper edge, and the torn edge returns as a divider over the footer video.
references.layout: About 2.5% margins. Sections carry red numbered mono labels at top-left. The layout changes every time: a label column with a product trio; a full-bleed black video; a horizontal row of tall category cards; a two-up split with a torn seam; a footer laid over video.

sections.description: New arrivals. The left 25% is a nearly empty column holding only a red numbered mono label at top, a bracketed link, and two tiny parenthesised notes further down. The right 60% holds three product images side by side with 4px gaps, each about 3:4, the middle one a tight crop of the same garment. Two carry a black brush-stroke tag with white condensed text in the top-left corner. Name and price sit under each in mono.

Categories as a horizontally scrolling row of five tall white cards, about 2:3 with 8px gaps, each showing a full-length cut-out model. The category name is set in the heavy condensed face rotated 90 degrees, running up the card's left edge from the bottom; a bracketed item count sits bottom-right in mono. The fifth card is cropped by the viewport edge.

Two-up split filling the viewport: two half-width photos of models on pale grounds, divided by a vertical torn-paper edge instead of a straight line. Each half has a category word in heavy condensed type at about 3.5vw bottom-left with a smaller parenthesised word attached like a suffix, and a bracketed count bottom-right.

A dark campaign video is cut off by a horizontal torn-paper edge, below which a taupe-grey ground holds the footer. Mono link clusters sit top-left and top-right. A cut-out model stands about 40% across, overlapping a very large condensed wordmark in darker grey so that letters pass behind her. Bottom-left, a subscribe line in white condensed type with a bracketed suffix; an underlined email field at right.

steal: Split one photograph along a torn-paper edge into a colour half and a greyscale half on different grounds, and let a two-word headline change colour across the same seam.
Run category names in heavy condensed type rotated 90 degrees up the edge of tall product cards, with a bracketed item count in mono at the opposite corner.
Reuse a torn-paper edge as the divider between sections and over the footer instead of straight lines.
